sections.body: Everything around us is made of matter. Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.
A SOLID keeps its shape. A rock, a spoon and ice are solids. 🧊
A LIQUID flows and takes the shape of its cup. Water and juice are liquids. 💧
A GAS spreads out to fill any space. The air we breathe is a gas. 🎈
Water can be all three! Ice (solid), water (liquid) and steam (gas).
With a grown-up: put an ice cube on a plate. Check it every 10 minutes. What happens?
Supervise any activity with hot water or steam. Ask 'does it keep its shape?' to help your child sort things.

hints: Which one takes the shape of a glass?
Juice is a liquid because it flows when you pour it. Find the one that flows.
quiz.explain: Milk flows and takes the shape of its glass, so it is a liquid.

quiz.q: Ice melting into water is a change from…
hints: Chocolate melting in your hand goes from hard (solid) to runny. Ice does the same.
quiz.explain: Ice is a solid. When it melts it becomes liquid water.

hints: A gas spreads out to fill space.
You often can't see a gas.
When you blow bubbles, the inside of each bubble is filled with something invisible. What is it?
quiz.explain: Air is a gas. It spreads out to fill the whole balloon.
